findings.description: SHEET-FORMULA-003's text formula-defines only ONE post-tax figure ('Net Unrealized = Unrealized P&L × (1 − Est. Tax Rate)'), yet its closing clause ('the post-tax columns shall be labelled estimates') is plural — implying at least two. The real code renders THREE tax-adjacent columns: 'Est. Tax Rate' (value input), 'Est. Unrealized Tax (est)' (=G{r}*H{r}, tested as a live formula in live_price_columns_are_formulas_others_are_values), and 'Net Unrealized (est)' (=G{r}*(1-H{r})). The spec text never names or defines 'Est. Unrealized Tax' at all. All three A-sketches, working from the spec text alone, unanimously produced only two output columns (a pre-tax P&L cell/formula and a single post-tax Net Unrealized formula) — none invented the middle 'Est. Unrealized Tax' column, because nothing in the given text calls for it. All three B-reconstructions independently and unanimously surfaced this exact column, its formula, and its '(est)' header suffix as pinned code behavior absent from the spec. Same gap, visible from both sides: a whole labelled-estimate column the spec's plural implies but never specifies, that A never builds and B has to reverse-engineer.

The spec is silent on what happens when 'Est. Tax Rate' is unavailable for a position (SHEET-FORMULA-003 states only the happy path). Real code has one specific, load-bearing answer: the rate cell is written as an empty string (`eff_rate.map(fmt_ppm).unwrap_or_default()`), and the two post-tax formulas — which are literal spreadsheet formulas referencing that same cell — let Sheets coerce the blank to 0, so 'Est. Unrealized Tax (est)' silently reads 0 and 'Net Unrealized (est)' silently degrades to exactly the pre-tax 'Unrealized P&L' figure (source comments explicitly name this a deliberate 'degrade'). All three B-runs converged tightly on this exact mechanism (B1 item 7, B2 item 9, B3 S1). Forced to invent a behavior for the same unstated case, the three A-runs produced three MUTUALLY INCOMPATIBLE answers: A1 defaults the rate to a Rust-side 0.0 (numerically lands on the same net-unrealized-equals-pnl outcome, but via a different mechanism — a literal 0 written into the cell, not a blank coerced by Sheets); A2 emits `=NA()`, an explicit spreadsheet ERROR — the opposite intent of a silent degrade; A3 replaces BOTH post-tax cells with a literal `"N/A"` string, breaking the live-formula structure for that row entirely. None of the three A answers matches the real mechanism, and they disagree with each other more than any other point in the six outputs — a genuine BD-DRIFT: spec silence that is invisible to a spec-only reader in a way that produces three incompatible guesses, while code+tests readers converge on the one real answer.

Every live-price-dependent Positions formula (Price, Market Value, Unrealized P&L, Est. Unrealized Tax (est), Net Unrealized (est), Unrealized %) is required — and explicitly tested (`per_row_formulas_reference_their_own_row_beneath_frozen_header`) — to reference ONLY its own row's cell addresses, asserting no other data row's `E{other}`/`B{other}` etc. ever appears in a row's formula text (an anti-row-shift invariant). SHEET-FORMULA-003's text says nothing about row-addressing or cross-row leakage. All three B-runs pinned this identically (B1 item 3, B2 item 5, B3 U5); it had no corresponding A-side signal since nothing in the given spec text could have prompted an A-run to address or omit it.

The spec states only that 'Est. Tax Rate' is 'the per-position effective unrealized tax rate written by tax' — no representation contract. Real code requires a specific, load-bearing encoding: a percent-suffixed STRING with exactly 4 fraction digits (`fmt_ppm`: `{sign}{whole}.{frac:04}%`, e.g. `Ppm(150_000)` → `"15.0000%"`), written as a Sheets `userEnteredValue` (never a forced string) specifically so Sheets coerces it to the numeric fraction that `=G*H`/`=G*(1-H)` can multiply — documented in the `batch_update_view` contract and exercised by `est_tax_rate_cell_is_numeric_percent_the_posttax_formulas_can_multiply`. All three B-runs pinned this format/coercion contract almost verbatim (B1 item 5, B2 items 7–8, B3 U6). None of the three A-sketches modeled this at all — all three treated `est_tax_rate` as a raw `f64` fraction, sidestepping the string-encoding/coercion problem the real implementation solves. This is a softer signal than findings 1–2 (more a granularity artifact of free-form sketches than a deliberate invented reading), but it is real code-side surplus directly relevant to the named requirement.

The Positions tab also carries an 'Unrealized %' column (`=IF(D{r}=0,0,G{r}/D{r})`, an explicit divide-by-zero guard), pinned by all three B-runs but never mentioned in SHEET-FORMULA-003's text. Weighted lower than findings 1–4: this figure sits outside the literal scope of the given requirement (pre-tax P&L / post-tax Net Unrealized) and is plausibly governed by a sibling EARS ID not included in this audit's excerpt, so it may not represent drift against THIS spec so much as evidence the excerpt is partial.

Two of three A-runs (A2, A3) read the spec's plural 'the post-tax columns shall be labelled estimates' as extending to the 'Est. Tax Rate' input column itself (labelling its header '(est.)'/'(estimate)'), while A1 did not. Real code does NOT label 'Est. Tax Rate' as an estimate — its header is the bare 'Est. Tax Rate' (POSITIONS_HEADER), distinct from the two suffixed 'Est. Unrealized Tax (est)' / 'Net Unrealized (est)' headers. The 2-of-3 majority reading diverges from the real implementation's choice, but since it isn't unanimous across A-runs it's a softer signal — a genuine spec ambiguity surfaced by disagreement rather than a clean forced-invention artifact.

notes:
Classification is BD-DRIFT on the strength of findings #1 and #2, where the identical gap is visible from both directions: the spec's plural 'post-tax columns... labelled estimates' names only one formula (Net Unrealized) and is silent on the missing-rate case, so A-runs (spec-only) either omit the unstated 'Est. Unrealized Tax' column entirely or invent three incompatible answers for the missing-rate degrade, while B-runs (code-only) converge tightly on both as pinned, tested behavior. Beyond those two BD findings, the B direction surfaces several additional surplus behaviors (row-anchoring invariant, exact percent-format/userEnteredValue coercion contract, Unrealized % column) that have no A-side counterpart at all — these are B-ONLY in isolation but don't change the overall classification since #1/#2 already establish BD-DRIFT.

Stability: B-runs are highly consistent — near-identical column letters (D/G/H/I/J/K), near-identical formula text, and independently-derived but matching descriptions of fmt_ppm's exact format and the degrade mechanism. The only B-internal wrinkle is scope disagreement on whether the DuplicateSymbolRow guard belongs to 'this concern' (B1 omits it, B2 treats it as core, B3 mentions but explicitly scopes it out as unrelated to pre/post-tax computation) — tangential to SHEET-FORMULA-003 itself, not counted as a primary finding.

A-runs agree strongly on the central mechanics (Net Unrealized must be a live, Sheets-recalculated formula, not Rust-computed, because 'sheets-view owns no accounting/tax math'; the multiplication direction G×(1−rate)) but diverge meaningfully on two secondary points: how to handle a missing/None tax rate (0.0 default vs `=NA()` error vs literal 'N/A' string — three different answers) and whether the 'labelled estimates' clause extends to the Est. Tax Rate header (1 vs 2 split). That mix of strong-core/weak-periphery agreement is why aAgreement is rated medium rather than high.
